rooms.name: Lighthouse Map Room
rooms.desc:
This is the immortal map room to the Haven Lighthouse. You can view one
of three maps; The House, the Cellar and Necromancer's Domain, and the
Subterranean Cavern and Sea Cave.

rooms.name: The Entrance to the Lighthouse
rooms.desc:
You are confronted by a medium sized room that appears to have been some
type of living area at one time. Pieces of broken furniture are scattered
around you, covered in faded white sheets in an attempt to protect them from
the layer of dust that now sits on the floor. Footprints leads from the door
to the east across the room to the west and into what looks like a hallway.
   The floorboards creek under your weight which is a worrying thought as the
lighthouse sits a good 80 feet above Haven bay and you are unsure as to the
integrity of the foundation. A flash of movement catches your eye but before
you realise what it was, it is gone. The room continues to the north, west
and south or you can walk back down the path to the east to Haven.

rooms.name: In the Keeper's House
rooms.desc:
This living area was actually the lower level of the lighthouse keeper's
residence and has been left to deteriorate without a full-time replacement.
Light filters in through the entrance to the south, the windows in this room
were long ago bricked up to keep the place from being looted. Square sections
on the walls mark the location of pictures that once hung here, perhaps in
an effort to liven the place up; it could certainly use it now as a feeling
of discomfort descends upon you.

rooms.name: In the Keeper's House
rooms.desc:
A small fireplace occupies this corner, half-burnt logs still sitting on
a metal frame within it. Outside, you can hear the sound of the wind which
howls around the lighthouse and this attached home, obviously highlighting
the need for the fireplace during the colder days and nights. Debris falls
from the roof, almost striking you before landing on the floor. Looking up,
you can see the support beams for the roof are in a terrible condition, quite
a few of them cracked and split.
   To the south, you can see a hallway that leads away from this main room.

rooms.name: In the Keeper's House
rooms.desc:
A narrow hallway to your west connects the main living area of the house
to the kitchen. Your footprints now join those which begin at the entrance
to the east and continue past you into the hallway. A single portrait has
been left within the room and hangs just to the left of the hallway entrance,
it's eyes following your every move...or so you think anyway.
   You're having trouble breathing in this area of the house, partly due to
the dusty environment and the very stale air. All sorts of fungii have
grown on the floor and walls, thriving in the moisture rich sea air.

rooms.name: In the Keeper's House
rooms.desc:
You almost trip over a few chunks of wood that once upon a time were a
chair. This area of the room appears to have been where food was served as is
evident by the round table that sits before you, remarkably still in one
piece although the damp sea air has slowly eaten it away over time. Chairs
covered with more sheets have been evenly placed around the table, scraps
of food still sitting on it.
   A small study adjoins the living area to teh south but before you can look
further, what feels like a hand rests on your shoulder causing you to spin
around wildly, only to find nothing there.

rooms.name: In the Keeper's House
rooms.desc:
Cool air circulates around you from a source that you cannot locate. It is
unusual, however, that the breeze doesn't disturb the layer of dust at your
feet nor does it move the moth-eaten curtains attached to the walls where
the windows once were. Moisture clings to your body and you can almost see
the floorboards and walls being eaten away by the mildew that has formed
over time.
   The entrance to the lighthouse lies to the north.

rooms.name: A Narrow Hallway
rooms.desc:
You stand in a narrow hallway that runs the length of the house. To your
south, you can see what looks like a small cloakroam while to the north, you
can access the lighthouse kitchen. The footprints from the east travel past
you and up the rickety stairs nearby.
   The remains of carpet line the hallway but the proximity to the sea has
left little to cover the floor. Cobwebs swing freely from almost every
corner you can see but their creators are no where to be found.

rooms.name: The Cloakroom
rooms.desc:
The room is actually larger than you first thought, large enough at least
for a person to stand here. The room was used to hang clothes, most likely
heavy jackets used by the keeper on his continual journey to the top of the
lighthouse. Now, nothing remains except the metal bars that run between the
walls.
   A narrow hallway to the north provides access to other areas of the
combined lighthouse and living area.

rooms.name: The Lighthouse Kitchen
rooms.desc:
The lighthouse kitchen must have been quite grand in its day, especially
since it was only required for a family of four people. Looking around now,
all you can are rusty pots and pans as well as a number of cobwebs strung
from various parts of the rooom. Water drips from a leaky tap and creates a
hollow sound each time it strikes the bottom of one of the kitchen sinks.
   The northern wall is curved as this room formed part of the original
lighthouse, now extended by the addition of the family house. Tracks on the
wall mark where water has travelled from the rooms above down to this lower
level.

rooms.name: The Lighthouse Kitchen
rooms.desc:
This end of the kitchen contains two large ovens, their combined width
spanning the entire wall. Cupboards above your head hold what is left of the
crockery used by the lighthouse residents, the majority of it now in hundreds
of little pieces.
   The kitchen extends to the east where you can return to the main living
area or you can travel through the door set in the northern wall, its surface
having been clawed by an unknown creature. Although this lighthouse has been
deserted for some years, you hear an occasional groan coming from the floor
above.

rooms.name: The Kitchen Pantry
rooms.desc:
This small room adjacent to the kitchen contains a number of shelves which
at one time would have been filled with foodstuffs. It also provides access
to the cellar below where the keeper doubtlessly stored a collection of
wines and ales. Although the lighthouse is only a short walk to the town of
Haven, rumor abounds about the recluse nature of the family that lived here
and the activities that were carried out behind closed doors.

rooms.name: The Study
rooms.desc:
Why a lighthouse keeper would have need for a study, you cannot fathom,
but you stand in one now. Loose sheets of paper lie on the floor, covered in
the same layer of dust that the remainder of this house contains. You're not
certain, but what looks like blood is splattered on the far wall and on the
tattered drapes that hang over another boarded up window.
   What sounds like something being dragged on the floor is coming from the
room to the north.

rooms.name: The Library
rooms.desc:
Some of the floorboards in this room are missing, revealing the rocky
foundation of this house. A few bookshelves cover the walls, although not
a book is to be found in this old library. You assume that there probably
wasn't a lot of books here to begin with and the remainder were most likely
stolen.

rooms.name: A Narrow Hallway
rooms.desc:
This hallway marks the entry to the second floor and continues to the
east and north. Rickety stairs lead down to the first level of the house
while a second set to the north probably lead up to the top of the
lighthouse.
   You shiver uncontrollably for just a few brief seconds as if someone
had traced a feather up and down your back but there is no one here.

rooms.name: Climbing the Spiral Staircase
rooms.desc:
You stand at the base of a spiral staircase that undoubtedly leads to the
top of the lighthouse. There are no windows here and the torches affixed
to the wall are literally dripping water, ensuring they won't be used again.
   Glancing over your shoulder, you notice a distinct change in the wall
structure. It is here that the house was attached to the brick lighthouse
and apparently no one got around to painting the walls a common color, not
that it really matters now.

rooms.name: A Narrow Hallway
rooms.desc:
This is the end of the hallway and except for the way back to the west,
there are only the doors to the north and south that allow exit from it. The
floor is covered by a very old and dirty carpet which is completely beyond
repair or salvage.

rooms.name: The Master Bedroom
rooms.desc:
This room has suffered the effects of damp and decay more than most in
the house. Mold grows in patches on the floor, walls and ceiling. There are
also many cobwebs but these too seem to be decaying. What remains of a bed
lies to the east and a smashed mirror hangs on the north wall.
   Many years ago, this bedroom would have been occupied by the keeper and
his wife but now it lies dormant and disused.

rooms.name: The Master Bedroom
rooms.desc:
Although you now stand on the second floor of the house, even the windows
at this level have been boarded up. However, the job was only completed
half-heartedly and has allowed the elements access to this room. An old
bed frame sits near the window, strips of cloth hanging from its top. Parts
of the mattress are still here although the mold has attacked it with vigor.

rooms.name: The Bedroom
rooms.desc:
The smaller of the two bedrooms in the house, this one was used by the
keeper's children. A few toys still sit on the floor but the remainder of the
room is empty. Cracks in the wall radiate out from a central location as if
a blunt object has been rammed into it. A window on the southern wall has,
like the others, been boarded up although gaps between the planks of wood
allow you to look across a small area of Haven bay.
   The door to the north leads to a narrow hallway and across that, the
door to the master bedroom. This room extends further to the east.

rooms.name: The Bedroom
rooms.desc:
You almost step on one of the children's toys which is embarrasing since
there is nothing else in this room to stumble over, giving you plenty of room
to move around. What you find disturbing is the blood stain on the floor
and the one on the wall. Perhaps the stories surrounding this house are
true but it is hard to accept the death of the children in their own room.

rooms.name: Climbing the Spiral Staircase
rooms.desc:
The spiral staircase continues in both directions, what looks like a small
hallway just below you. Cracks in the wall are cause for alarm, especially
if you wish to continue your climb but after all, the lighthouse has remained
standing for a long time.

rooms.name: Climbing the Spiral Staircase
rooms.desc:
Just above your head, a wooden ceiling spans the entire width of the
lighthouse although a small square cut into it provides access to the top
of the tower. The stairs travel from the hole and continue down to the
keeper's house.

rooms.name: At the Top of the Lighthouse
rooms.desc:
The room is completely enclosed by glass, apart from the roof above you.
In the center of the floor, a large silver dish rotates slowly powered by a
mechanical device of sorts. A glowing gemstone sits in front of the dish
and provides the necessary light, however, it sits high above the floor level
and you are unable to reach it. Gaps in the roof have allowed numerous
storms to aid in the deterioration of this room, mainly the wooden floorboards
which break under your steps.
   A trapdoor set in the floor is the only safe exit from the room.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
Either the lighthouse keeper really loved his wine or this cellar was
used as a storage area for Haven. This area is quite large and could more
than easily handle the needs of the family living in the house above you.
   The cellar is divided into four chambers, each sub-divided into a number
of rows by the wine racks that extend from the floor to the ceiling. The walls
are made of rock since the cellar has been built into the cliff foundation
that the lighthouse sits on. Stairs lead up from here to the ground floor
of the house.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
The corner of this chamber is practically falling apart, the rock wall
has a large crack in it that extends to the floor. Water seeps in from above
you and pools on the ground before disappearing into the crack. The chamber
continues to the west and south.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
The air is musty and damp here, obviously this room does not see a lot
of ventilation. Light streams in through a hole in the wall to the east
where you can see a rather large wine barrel. The door to the south leads
back into one of the cellar chambers.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
The ground crumbles beneath you as you walk further to the east and you
discover that the hole in the wall is merely a part of the degradation that
is happening in this area. Cracks radiate from the hole in all directions
and you must be careful not to stand to closely or the entire section may
give way.
   A barrel over six feet tall and 3 feet wide sits against the far wall,
only a small tap on its face allows access to the contents.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
Barrels and barrels of wine have been stacked against the far wall and
look precariously close to falling over. Mildew has set in and a few of the
barrels have become rotten, wine dripping out in numerous places and onto
the ground. You can weave your way between the wine racks to the north or
to the east.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
You stand at the north western intersection of the four wine cellar
chambers. From here, you can access the chambers to the south and east or
travel back into the chamber to the north. Dust falls from the ceiling as
if someone was walking in the rooms above you, but you can't hear a sound
except that of your own breathing.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
The entry to the second chamber leaves you standing before two doors; one
to the north and one to the east. Both look fairly solid which is unusual
given the amount of rotting wood that surrounds you in the form of broken
wine racks.
   To the west and south, you can access another of the chambers down here
in the wine cellar.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
This small room has only one exit, the one to the west from where you
came. It contains nothing at all and you cannot see a purpose for it,
especially since the door was locked.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
You weave and crawl your way through the wine racks and end up in the
coner of the chamber. The ground is soft and spongy, a carpet of moss having
grown here over time. You wouldn't have thought the wine could provide
nutrients to plant life, but perhaps it does...

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
This is the south western intersection of the four wine cellar chambers.
Wine racks travel from the northern wall to the southern wall within this
chamber and you find it difficult to move between them. Broken bottles of
wine still remain in the racks, their contents spilled long ago leaving no
trace.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
You step on a small clump of mushrooms that have sprouted up from the
floor. It looks as if the foundation of this cellar is not entirely rock
which is a worrying though since you now stand in it. You can access two of
the other chambers to the north and west. Large barrels sit flush against
the eastern and southern walls.

rooms.name: In a Large Barrel
rooms.desc:
Remarkable and also very clever. This barrel is something of a primitive
safe, although whoever placed it here has emptied it out. You can still smell
the wine that this barrel once contained and you begin to feel light headed
as the fumes take effect. The only exit is through the barrel opening to the
west.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
Two large metal storage bins sit against the western wall, both of them
empty. The racks impede your progress throughout the chamber but you can
squeeze past a few of them to the north or east if you desire.

rooms.name: The Wine Cellar
rooms.desc:
It looks as if someone has been doing work on the sub-structure here
recently. Large chunks of rock and wood lie in a heap on the ground, the
eastern wall appearing to be the source. As you move closer, several smaller
stones drop onto the floor and sound echoes throughout the wine cellar.

rooms.name: In a Large Barrel
rooms.desc:
There is more than meets the eye here as you stand within the barrel
itself. You have stumbled across a secret room of sorts which exits into
the wine cellar to the north and continues further to the east where you
can see a set of stairs leading to the level below.

rooms.name: In a Large Barrel
rooms.desc:
The wood of the wine barrel gives way to the rock of the lighthouse
foundation. Stairs cut deeper into the rock lead down into the darkness
while the barrel stretches away to the west and then into one of the cellar
chambers.

rooms.name: A Long Passageway
rooms.desc:
You estimate that you must be at least 40 feet below the level of the
house and you wonder how much further this sub-structure extends. Obviously,
this area was unknown to the lighthouse keeper and his family as is apparent
by the relatively intact walls and lack of dust.
   Stairs lead up to the wine cellar and the passageway continues to the east
into the darkness.

rooms.name: A Long Passageway
rooms.desc:
Two rooms can be accessed from here, one to the south and a larger one
to the north. In the distance to the east you can hear a cry for help and
what can only be described as the sound of intense pain; a scream so high
pitched and loud that it cuts through you like a knife.

rooms.name: The Necromancers' Meditation Area
rooms.desc:
You are confronted by a single room with a number of bookshelves against
each wall and a pedestal in the middle. Arcane symbols have been drawn on
the ground and you can almost feel the evil radiating from this room. You
can return to the passageway through the opening to the north.

rooms.name: The Necromancers' Laboratory
rooms.desc:
You stand at the entrance to what can only be described as a laboratory
of some type. Shelves to your left contain a number of glass jars and vials
while a large table further to the east has bits and pieces on it that you
can't quite see from here.
   The laboratory extends to the north and east while the passageway lies
to the south.

rooms.name: The Necromancers' Laboratory
rooms.desc:
Some type of glass contraption occupies this corner of the lab. A strange
red liquid is taken from one of three barrels before it passes through a
number of glass containers, some of them heated by a single flame. The
resultant mixture is combined with other equally strange liquids and empties
into a vial.

rooms.name: The Necromancers' Laboratory
rooms.desc:
The entire eastern wall of the laboratory is taken up by a large table.
It has on it a number of small piles, most of which you do not recognise
but assume must be ingredients of some sort. The laboratory extends to the
west and south.

rooms.name: The Necromancers' Laboratory
rooms.desc:
The entire eastern wall of the laboratory is taken up by a large table.
At this end of the table, you recognise human body parts and fail to comprehend
what possible purpose they serve. Whoever uses this laboratory is certainly
insanse to deal in experimentation like this.

rooms.name: A Long Passageway
rooms.desc:
The passageway continues to the west and east of here, while the way
to the south is barred by a heavy door. You can hear someone whimpering
from inside the room but your attempts to speak to them go unanswered.

rooms.name: A Prison Cell
rooms.desc:
You are confronted by a small, dark and musty prison cell. Chains hang
from the walls, some of them still restrain both living and dead victims.
Several pairs of beady red eyes stare at you from the darkness but stay just
out of sight. The passageway lies to the north while the cell continues to
the east.

rooms.name: A Prison Cell
rooms.desc:
This end of the cell has pretty much of the same as the other end, although
there are a few more creatures here chained to the wall. Some of them call out
to you in a language you don't understand and try as you might, you cannot
break the shackles that keep them here. A pile of straw lies in the corner
and the prison cell extends to the west.

rooms.name: A Long Passageway
rooms.desc:
The passageway bends here, travelling to the north and to the west. The
air feels almost electric and the hairs on the back of your neck rise
instinctivly as if you are about to be struck by lightning. A piercing scream
to the north grabs your attention before the silence again descends around
you.

rooms.name: A Long Passageway
rooms.desc:
You have reached one end of the passageway, this end terminating in doors
to the north and east. A sickly odor wafts around the passageway and you are
having trouble identifying what it is and where it is coming from, but the
door to the east is the more likely of the two.

rooms.name: A Torture Chamber
rooms.desc:
The sight before you is like none you have ever seen before. If a place
of eternal torment existed, then this would most likely be it - this room
is a torture chamber and from the looks of it, has been widely and recently
used. Wooden and mechanical devices fill the floor space and still contain
bodyparts and a covering of fresh blood. What remains of one poor creature
has been stuffed into a barrel in the corner, a makeshift coffin of sorts.
   Before you exit to the west, you are overwhelmed by a sense of torment
and anguish which, in such a place, is not hard to believe. It's as if the
lives lost in here have remained, unable to escape into any form of afterlife.

rooms.name: The Chambers of the Necromancer
rooms.desc:
If fear and evilness were tangible quantities, this chamber abounds in
both of them. Two human skulls levitate at the entrance, each emitting a
soft light that is rather inadequate for a chamber of this size. The floor
is covered by a plush carpet and the rock walls have been highly polished,
a painstaking process you imagine.
   To the east you can see what looks like an altar while to the north,
a single bookshelf and desk rest against the far wall. You can enter a dark
passageway through the door to the south.

rooms.name: The Chambers of the Necromancer
rooms.desc:
A large altar has been carved out of the rock and placed in front of where
you now stand. It is covered by a silk cloth and has a variety of arcane
symbols drawn upon it. Candles have been evenly spaced around the top of the
altar and a strange dagger has been impaled in the middle of them all.
   The chamber continues to the north and to the west.

rooms.name: The Chambers of the Necromancer
rooms.desc:
This area has been set aside as a private study.  A desk has been pushed
up against the northern wall and a small bookshelf sits next to it.  The desk
is bare except for a container of ink, a quill pen and a single tome.

rooms.name: The Chambers of the Necromancer
rooms.desc:
The only item in this corner of the chamber is the wooden coffin before
you. You could be mistaken, but it looks as if the Necromancer chooses to
sleep within it although the reason why is unclear. It has been constructed
from a dark wood and has golden handles on either side to aid in its
movement.

rooms.name: Climbing a Ladder
rooms.desc:
You are halfway along a ladder that leads into a small room above you and
down into the murky darkness below. You soon discover that you are working
your way through a layer of rock, this area having been carved out to allow
access between the different sub-structure areas.

rooms.name: At the Base of a Ladder
rooms.desc:
You are at the base of a wooden ladder that reaches skyward into the
darkness. To the west, a large rock cavern contains a number of crates,
barrels and general sea-going equipment. From here, you can see tunnels
leading away from the main chamber deeper into the rock foundation.

rooms.name: A Subterranean Cavern
rooms.desc:
The eastern end of the cavern is cluttered with all manner of objects but
mostly crates, which upon closer inspection reveal chunks of metal. Each
crate bares an insignia of some sort; some the royal seal of Amber, others
the seal of Mistkeep, and yet others the crest of Kir Oshi. The ground is a
combination of rock and sand, showing telltale signs of pedestrian traffic.
   To the east, you can see a small opening in the cavern wall while in most
other directions, tunnels branch off into other areas.

rooms.name: A Small Tunnel
rooms.desc:
A strong breeze circles around you as you work your way through this small
passage. Other tunnels at ground level lead to other parts of this subterranean
structure but you are too large to fit into any of them. Listening carefully,
you can hear the sound of the sea through one of the tunnels in the eastern
wall.
   A large cavern lies to the west while the tunnel continues to the south.

rooms.name: A Subterranean Cavern
rooms.desc:
You weave your way through several cloth bundles but find nothing of
interest in this corner of the cavern. Looking above you, the ceiling is
barely visible and any sound echos quite distinctly around the area. The
cavern opens out to the north and west while a small tunnel leaves east
from here.

rooms.name: A Subterranean Cavern
rooms.desc:
Standing near the center of the cavern and looking around, you are in awe
at the sheer size of this place. It's hard to believe that high above you,
the Haven lighthouse has been constructed. The cavern continues to the south
and east while to your west, a tunnel disappears into the darkness. You
have difficulty seeing over the amount of goods stored here.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
You stand at what could be the beginning or the end of a lengthy tunnel
system, depending on your point of view. Over time, the sea has eroded the
rocky walls in this place leaving many interconnecting passageways, although
the majority are too small for any creature to fit into. You can, however,
access a large cavern to the south or progress further into the tunnels to
the north or west.

rooms.name: A Subterranean Cavern
rooms.desc:
Walking in this area requires slightly more effort, the rocky floor
giving way to sand and impeding your progress around the cavern. For that
reason, it is relatively clear of items and allows easy access to the
remainder of the cavern to the north and east.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
Casks of ale have been stacked haphazardly before you and you're careful
not to disturb them. The tunnel bends here and it appears as if the walls
to the south are converging, making travel in that direction difficult but
not impossible.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
You almost bump your head on the tunnel roof as you follow the twists and
turns through the rock structure. The air feels relatively dry and free from
humidity which is odd given the proximity to the sea that you can hear echo
through the tunnels.
   A T-junction in the system allows you to travel west, east or south.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
The sound of the sea grows stronger as you maneuver your way across rolled
up ship sails. Hessian bags sit alongside the tunnel wall along with a
transport platform of some type. The tunnel extends to the east and west.

rooms.name: A Subterranean Cavern
rooms.desc:
You have arrived at the top of a set of stairs that have been carved out
of the rock wall and floor. A tunnel leads away to the east and you will have
to step over a large number of assorted items if you wish to travel in that
direction. The sound and smell of the ocean is quite strong here and eminates
from the base of the stairs.

rooms.name: A Small Alcove
rooms.desc:
You are in a small alcove adjacent to a large cave to the west that opens
onto the ocean. A sandy beach, also to the west, sits alongside the edge
of the cave while a set of stairs leads up from here.

rooms.name: A Large Sea Cave
rooms.desc:
The beach upon which you stand extends to the north and south along the
eastern edge of this large cave. Further to the north west, the mouth of
the cave meets the ocean while further to the west, you can see some kind
of ship berthed at a wooden dock.

rooms.name: A Large Sea Cave
rooms.desc:
The northern end of the beach meets the cave wall to the north and east
while the calm waters of the cave lagoon lie to the west. Although this area
may have been naturally created, it has undergone quite a few modifications
including the dock to the south west and the small alcove just to the south
east of here.

rooms.name: A Large Sea Cave
rooms.desc:
The southern end of the beach meets the cave wall to the east and south
while a wooden dock stretches into the cave lagoon west of here. Although
this area may have been naturally created, the dock is a sure sign that
others visit this place frequently.
   Towards the end of the dock, you can see a medium sized ship.

rooms.name: A Large Sea Cave
rooms.desc:
The dock here is only a few feet off the ground and you wonder how the
ship at the western end could sail in here and not get caught on the sandy
bottom of the lagoon. The calm waters lap at the base of the dock and onto
the beach to the east.

rooms.name: A Large Sea Cave
rooms.desc:
You have reached the end of the dock and can only progress west onto the
ship, travel east along the dock or north to enter the waters of the cave
lagoon. Looking northward, the open ocean beckons through the mouth of the
cave.

rooms.name: The Upper Deck
rooms.desc:
It's not until you are aboard this ship do you realise that the flag it
flies is that of a skull and crossbones. Judging by the relatively small
size of this ship, it has been designed for speed rather than cargo carrying
capability although by the looks of it, the ship can hold quite a few tons
of goods.

rooms.name: The Upper Deck
rooms.desc:
You skirt around a large hole in the middle of the ship which appears
to be an access point for the loading and unloading of cargo. A wooden crane
system has been erected to lift goods from the cargo hold and swing them
out onto the dock. The ship rocks gently in the waters of the lagoon but you
can only travel to the north or south along the deck.

rooms.name: The Upper Deck
rooms.desc:
The stern of the ship is wide and open with the wheel clearly visible on
a raised platform further aft. A narrow doorway leads to a set of stairs
which allow access to the lower deck.

rooms.name: The Sea Cave Lagoon
rooms.desc:
The water is quite pleasant as you swim around near the beach to the east.
A school of small fish swims nearby, not afraid of your intrusion into
their domain. The lagoon is shallow here and you can easily stand on the
bottom but it deepens rapidly to the west.
   You can climb onto a wooden dock to the south or swim further around the
lagoon to the north and west.

rooms.name: The Sea Cave Lagoon
rooms.desc:
You splash around in the shallow waters of the lagoon, a nice sandy beach
directly east of here. The cave wall blocks any travel to the north and you
can just see the ocean through the cave mouth to the west. The lagoon extends
to the south and west.

rooms.name: The Sea Cave Lagoon
rooms.desc:
You have reached the mouth of a large sea cave, the calm waters of the
cave lagoon to the south and east. To your north, the ocean waves crash
against the outside of the cave walls but surprisingly have no effect on the
waters here. Further to the east, a sandy beach hugs the eastern wall of the
cave while to the south, a wooden dock extends from the beach to a medium
sized ship.

rooms.name: The Sea Cave Lagoon
rooms.desc:
The lagoon is quite deep here which makes sense given the ship that is
docked to the west. The cave provides a fantastic hiding place and obviously
someone has used that to their advantage. You cannot climb onto the ship
from here, but you can scramble onto the dock to the south or travel further
around the lagoon to the north or east.

rooms.name: The Lower Deck
rooms.desc:
The lower deck of the ship is quite cramped and you have to be careful
to avoid bumping your head on the beams. You can travel into the cargo hold
to the south or through a door to your west. Stairs lead upwards to the top
deck.

rooms.name: The Lower Deck
rooms.desc:
The remainder of the ship from here to the south is used to store all
manner of goods. A hole in the upper deck allows access to the cargo stored
here.

rooms.name: The Lower Deck
rooms.desc:
You are at the bow of the ship, albeit below the upper deck. Progress
further south is blocked by several large containers so your only exit is
to travel back to the north.

rooms.name: The Captain's Quarters
rooms.desc:
Apparently, only the captain of this vessel has any personal space at all
and even that is fairly cramped. This small room contains nothing more than
a bunk and a table in the corner. A single porthole on the western side gives
a nice view of the cave wall.

rooms.name: A Secret Compartment
rooms.desc:
The trapdoor above opens into this small room big enough to hold only
one person. More of the arcane symbols grace the walls and the floor and
you feel drawn to the middle of the room by some magical force. It requires
great effort to move anywhere but from the position you are in.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
The floor gently slopes down from the east and on more than one occassion,
you lose your footing as you travel along the tunnel. It bends here, continuing
up the slope to the east and also further to the south.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
Shadows jump at you from the many openings in the tunnel walls but you
convince your self they are simply a part of your active imagination and
a product of the tunnel creation. A blast of fresh sea air hits you from the
west and you can smell, rather than see, stagnant water to the south.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
You stand at what could be the beginning or the end of a lengthy tunnel
system, depending on your point of view. Sounds echo around you, carried
through a series of smaller tunnels, the majority of which are too small for
any creature to fit into. You can, however, access a large cavern to the east
or progress further into the tunnels to the north.
   You can just make out a pool of stagnant water to the south and decide it
may not be wise to travel in that direction.

rooms.name: Swimming in a Stagnant Pool
rooms.desc:
Defying the laws of nature and science, this pool has spawned a type
of algae which continues to flourish here despite the lack of food, fresh
water and light. The smell is almost overpowering and it would be wise not
to remain here for too long.

rooms.name: Swimming in a Stagnant Pool
rooms.desc:
Swimming through this mess is almost impossible, it is so thick in places
that you might as well walk on top of it. You can't even see the bottom
from here and wonder how deep this area really goes.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
A vortex of sea air engulfs you and is then gone as quickly as it arrived.
You can see a faint glow coming from the tunnel to the south and the sounds
of the sea are strong here, leading you to believe the exit from this system
is nearby. You can travel to the west, south or east into the tunnels.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
You trip on a barely visible rock and bang your head onto the rock wall in
front of you. Slightly dazed, you stand and see that the tunnel ends here,
the only exit back to the north. Cursing the rock that caused you to trip,
you decide to continue.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
You eyes slowly adjust to the combination of a small amount of light and
the surrounding darkness. The light comes from the tunnel to the west while
the darkness extends into the tunnels to the north and south.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
The tunnel turns sharply to the south and ends in a rock wall. Given the
nature of this system, you could search for hours and never find a way out
or it could take only a few minutes and you would be free from the confines
of the tunnels. For now, you can only travel back to the east.

rooms.name: Swimming in a Stagnant Pool
rooms.desc:
You swim further into the depths of the pool and arrive at a dead end.
The cavern walls are covered in a thick layer of the algae and any thought
you had of climbing out of the pool should be forgotten. The only exit is
to swim back the way you came.

rooms.name: A Small Tunnel
rooms.desc:
You squeeze your way through a narrow opening in the rocky walls and find
yourself at a dead end anyway. Not only that, but you are now standing in
ankle high sea water that has seeped in through the sandy floor. It appears
as if the only exit is back the way you came from.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
The end of the tunnel is littered with what look like human bones. They
have been neatly sorted according to type, some even packaged ready for
transport to an unknown destination. You can't imagine what type of creature
would deal in the trade of human bones but the proof lies before you.
   The tunnel to the north provides the only exit.

rooms.name: A Tunnel System
rooms.desc:
The tunnel doesn't progress too much further before ending in a wall of
rock. However, much work has been completed here to turn this area into
something of a food preparation area. A large cauldron sits over an open fire
while cooking tools hang from the wall. Slabs of rock serve as bench tops
and it looks as if someone is in the middle of cooking the next meal.
